scope: R205: the encoder switch is a single config item, and the pinned-memory concern from R203/R204 was based on a wrong model
decisive_log_evidence: layerwise_backend.py:363 Enabled rank-local layerwise offload for encoder text_encoder (77 blocks across 2 stacks)
confirms_r203: both the text encoder and the DiT use layerwise offload, so the encoder takes the manual-component-offload path that loads on entry and offloads on exit, re-streaming 63 GB per encode_prompt call

refutes_r203_r204_core_worry.my_wrong_model: DiT 62 GB plus encoder 63 GB both pinned equals 125 GB against a 94.3 GiB limit, short by 22 GiB
refutes_r203_r204_core_worry.reality: layerwise offload means only one block is in the pinned buffer at any time, so per block it is 63 GB / 77 = about 0.82 GB and the pinned need is roughly 1-2 GB
refutes_r203_r204_core_worry.verdict: the pinned limit was never the blocker; the scheme-B reasoning in R203 section 4d and R204 is withdrawn
still_valid: about 99 percent of encoder time is transfer
per-call loading makes 3.15 s a hard floor

facts: DEFAULT_OFFLOAD_COMPONENTS = {dit} - the default already excludes the text encoder
should_offload_component returns resolved.offloads(component) under layer-wise strategies
the_real_switch.consumer: pipeline_minimax_h3.py:1438 _uses_manual_component_offload gates the load/offload path, otherwise load_to_device with the comment Keep Qwen resident
the_real_switch.nature: a configuration change, not a code change and not a kernel change

must_verify_not_assume: device memory: encoder resident 7.33 GiB per rank plus the DiT layerwise blocks; the earlier 18.97 GiB figure used a DiT peak measured without a resident encoder, so it needs measurement
whether Module.to truly releases the host copy, though this matters less now that pinning is known not to be the constraint
whether the DLO setup needs the memory freed by the encoder offload; if DiT peak plus resident encoder exceeds 32 GiB it will OOM, and that is the only real risk
headline_value: downgrades the work from writing code or a kernel to changing one config item, and removes a false bottleneck I had invented myself
